description: A foundational safety course covering proper ladder usage, inspection, setup, and fall prevention.

slides.title: Welcome to Ladder Safety
slides.text: This course will teach you how to inspect, set up, and safely climb ladders. Ladder accidents cause thousands of injuries every year.

slides.title: Why Ladder Safety Matters
slides.text: Falls from ladders can cause serious injury. Always follow proper ladder procedures and inspect equipment before use.

slides.title: Important Safety Rule
slides.text: Never use a ladder that is damaged, bent, or missing parts.

slides.title: Ladder Setup Demonstration
slides.text: Watch this short video demonstrating proper ladder setup.

slides.title: Steps to Inspect a Ladder
steps: Check the ladder rails for cracks or bends.
Inspect the rungs for damage or looseness.
Check ladder feet for wear or missing rubber.
Make sure locks and spreaders function correctly.

slides.title: Three Points of Contact
slides.text: Always maintain three points of contact when climbing a ladder. This helps maintain balance and stability.

points.text: Ladder feet must be placed on solid, level ground.
Never stand on the top rung.
Keep your body centered between the rails.

slides.question: How many points of contact should you maintain when climbing a ladder?
slides.correctText: Correct. Three points of contact keeps you stable.
slides.incorrectText: Incorrect. The correct answer is three.

slides.question: It is safe to stand on the top rung of a ladder.
slides.correctText: Correct. Standing on the top rung is unsafe.
slides.incorrectText: Incorrect. Standing on the top rung is dangerous.

slides.question: You see a ladder placed on uneven ground. What should you do?

slides.title: Common Ladder Hazards
slides.text: Common ladder hazards include unstable ground, overreaching, damaged rungs, and using the wrong ladder for the job.

slides.question: When should a ladder be inspected?
You should keep your belt buckle between ladder rails while climbing.

slides.title: Safe Ladder Climbing Procedure
steps: Do not carry tools in your hands.

slides.question: What should you do if a ladder is damaged?
options: Report and remove it from service

slides.title: Final Safety Reminder
slides.text: Always use the right ladder for the job and inspect it before every use.

slides.title: Course Complete
slides.text: Congratulations! You have completed the Ladder Safety Training course.
